identify: Disc brakes and thru-axles, one central riser carrying a bridge with both pads and extensions, on an AeroDrive base bar with the stem built in. Launched January 2025; the Liv Avow Advanced SL is the women's version of the same bike. Not the rim-brake Trinity Advanced Pro (two pad stacks), and not the 2011–2015 rim-brake bike with the same name.

cockpit.steerer: Full-composite steerer. Tri frameset ships with a long fork (High position), TT frameset with a short fork (Low position); converting Tri to TT means cutting the steerer, which Giant calls irreversible.
cockpit.stem: Integrated: Giant base bar with integrated stem combination (AeroDrive); no stem length options.
cockpit.stack_system: Eight 10 mm spacers under the bridge: 0–80 mm in 10 mm steps. The Tri frameset comes with a long fork (high front) and the TT frameset with a short one, about 47 mm apart in pad height; cutting a Tri fork down to TT cannot be undone.
cockpit.reach_system: The pads flip front to back and bolt in several holes: 11 positions over 75 mm, 7.5 mm apart. The extensions slide 0–93 mm. Owners and fitters say pad reach is the tight limit on this bike.
cockpit.angle_system: Wedges of 0°, 10° and 15° come with the bike.
cockpit.notes: Armrest width 8 positions 192-244 mm; extension width 82/102/146/166 mm; armrest length 125 mm. Owners and fitters say stock pad reach is the main limit (mono-riser sits only slightly ahead of the steerer); one size-M owner needed aftermarket reach parts. No XL; L tops out at 455 mm (Tri) / 470 mm (TT) back-of-pad reach at 0 deg.

effect.text: Carbon replacement for the stock extension bridge. Giant Japan: up to 50 mm further forward and 25 mm further back than the stock bridge, same lateral range. Giant Australia/Denmark instead say 50 mm forward and 50 mm wider.

evidence.says: Compatible with MY25+ Giant Trinity and Liv Avow aero cockpits; extension range 50 mm further forward and 50 mm wider than the previous bridge; RRP AUD 399.99.
Full-carbon bridge for Trinity and Liv Avow; up to 50 mm forward and 25 mm rearward vs the standard bridge, lateral unchanged; JPY 44,000.
DKK 2,099; this page's compatibility line names Giant Propel and Liv Avow (inconsistent with the other regions).

parts.needs: Kit contents not listed; confirm with a Giant dealer (regional pages disagree on details).

parts.model: Extension adapter plate for Giant Trinity 2025 mono handlebar (TRINITY-MONO-PLATE)

effect.text: Replaces the stock base plate on the mono-riser with a forward-curved plate whose extension mounts sit ahead of the riser (stock mounts sit behind). About 35 mm more forward reach, according to FastTT in an e-mail a rider shared; the product page gives no figure. Has a threaded BTA mount.

evidence.says: Maker's description: designed specifically for the Giant Trinity 2025 mono handlebar, not older models; for FastTT extensions, other brands to be checked; forward-curved shape for extra reach.

User relays FastTT: the new-Trinity plate adds around 35 mm forward reach; another notes its mounts sit forward of the riser and Di2 wires then run outside over the plate; a third expects stock extensions to fit (not confirmed).

parts.needs: FastTT extensions (others unconfirmed); Di2/eTap wires route externally over the plate.

effect.text: Mounts AeroCoach Ascalon extensions on the disc Trinity cockpit. Reach/stack offset not published.

evidence.says: Lists a 'Giant Trinity (disc brake)' adapter option (+GBP 285 over the GBP 115 base) separate from the rim-brake Trinity tilt-block option; warranty only with Ascalon extensions.

parts.needs: AeroCoach Ascalon extensions. Price shown as a GBP 115 base plus a GBP 285 option charge; total not confirmed.

parts.model: Reach adaptor (+50 mm) for the new Trinity

effect.text: Owner of a size M fitted it because stock pad reach was too short.

evidence.says: Owner (178 cm, size M) does not use the stock base plate; added a Fouriers +50 mm adaptor and FastTT reversible extender plates for more reach.

effect.text: Used together with a reach adaptor to push the extensions forward; offset not stated.

evidence.says: Same owner runs FastTT reversible extender plates on his new Trinity for more reach.

effect.text: Seen on a pro's race bike (Gustav Iden, Nice 2025) with TriRig hydration mounts. How the extensions mount to the SYNC bridge is not described.

evidence.says: Slowtwitch bike feature: Iden's new Trinity runs Ride Sync Aerobar 3 extensions; sponsored pro bike, mounting hardware not described.

parts.reason_incompatible: Base bar and stem are one integrated Giant part; Giant says the cockpit is designed for its base bar with SYNC extensions. Launch coverage and forum users note no option for a non-proprietary front end.

evidence.says: Stem spec: Giant base bar with integrated stem combination; cockpit designed for Giant Base Bar with SYNC EVO Pro extensions.
Launch feature lists the still-integrated, proprietary front end as a con.
Tall rider wants a non-proprietary front end and notes none is offered.

effect.text: Made for the previous twin-stack cockpit.

parts.reason_incompatible: Maker's description limits it to dual-mount Trinity models 2015-2024 with the original spacer stacks; the 2025 mono-riser needs the separate TRINITY-MONO-PLATE.

evidence.says: Plate is for Giant Trinity dual-mount models 2015-2024 fitted with the original spacers.

gaps: Extension clamp diameter, base-bar dimensions and armrest bolt pattern are not given in Giant's fitting guide or product pages; no owner measurement found. Whether standard 22.2 mm extensions or third-party armrests bolt to the SYNC clamps is unconfirmed.
Giant 'SYNC EVO Pro' extensions, spare riser spacers, wedges and armrests as separately sold parts: no Giant product page or part number found.
A second FastTT listing ('Giant Trinity 2025 centre mount', materiel-velo ref 1891634) exists but the page did not load its product text; unclear whether it differs from the mono plate.
FastTT's 35 mm reach figure comes only from a forum relay of an email; no FastTT page states it. FastTT's own website was not found; only retailer copies of the maker text.

Reversible stock base plate (more reach) is known only via a forum relay of Matt Bottrill's YouTube video; Giant's guide does not show it and no mm figure is given (a fitter guessed about 460 mm max pad reach on an M).
Fouriers +50 mm adaptor: no product page or listing found; single owner mention.

TriRig: pros run TriRig BTS/hydration mounts on this bike, but no TriRig fit part (riser, plate) for the Trinity mono-riser was found; TriRig's universal BTA plate is too wide for one owner's narrow cups.
AeroCoach tilt-block adapters list only the rim-brake Trinity; whether any AeroCoach tilt block suits the disc Trinity beyond the Ascalon disc option is unconfirmed.

Giant's Trinity Cockpit Extender Kit: regional pages disagree (Denmark lists Propel and Avow; Japan says +50 forward/+25 back; Australia +50 forward/+50 wider); no US/CA/EU price in EUR, kit contents or part number found; no owner report yet.
Owner reports for this generation are very few (two identifiable owners on Slowtwitch as of Nov 2026).
MY27 adds an XXS (Liv Avow geometry) with pad ranges in the Avow guide; not included here.
